notice: Listing a source does not mean its raw data has been downloaded or integrated.

sources.title: NASA Human Research Program Risks
sources.supports: Evidence-based descriptions of cardiovascular, sleep, fitness, immune, behavioral, ocular and radiation risks.
sources.limitations: Research and risk context only. Does not provide astronaut-level continuous vital recordings or clinical thresholds.

sources.title: NASA HRP Five Hazards
sources.supports: The five exploration hazards: radiation, isolation and confinement, distance, gravity and hostile or closed environments.
sources.limitations: Supports hazard explanations, not cabin telemetry or operational alert policies.

sources.title: NASA HRP Ongoing Research
sources.supports: Research areas and measurement approaches that can inform indicator selection.
sources.limitations: Does not provide downloadable data for every research activity described.

sources.title: Canadian Space Agency: Monitoring Radiation and Astronaut Health
sources.supports: Radiation monitoring context and space radiation instruments, including CANS.
sources.limitations: Does not provide a patient-level radiation time series or personal dose recommendations.

sources.title: Canadian Space Agency: Why Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
sources.supports: Background on long-duration spaceflight, microgravity, radiation and isolation.
sources.limitations: General science context; not a numerical astronaut vital-sign dataset.

sources.title: NASA OSDR Environmental Data Application
sources.supports: Environmental measurements such as CO2, temperature, relative humidity and radiation from selected ISS experiments or hardware.
sources.limitations: Confirm mission, sensor location, units and sampling interval before use. Environmental readings must not automatically be presented as personal astronaut exposure.

sources.title: NASA OSDR RadLab
sources.supports: Radiation instrument readings and historical radiation context from ISS and beyond-LEO platforms.
sources.limitations: Instrument readings must not be presented as an individual's personal dose or health risk.

sources.title: NASA NLSP UTMB Bedrest Campaign 1 Actigraphy
sources.supports: Sleep-related measures such as sleep duration, latency and efficiency in a bed-rest analog study.
sources.limitations: Ground-based bed-rest participants, not astronauts sleeping in space. Actual files and access conditions still require verification.

sources.title: NASA OSDR Study OSD-575
sources.supports: Serum metabolic, immune and cardiac-related biomarker research context.
sources.limitations: Sample-based measurements, not continuous wearable readings. Verify individual files and sampling details before use.

sources.title: NASA Human Research Program Standard Measures
sources.supports: Standardized categories for sleep, activity, cognition, blood, urine and fitness measurements.
sources.limitations: Not all astronaut records are publicly downloadable.

sources.title: NASA Human Research Roadmap Evidence Reports
sources.supports: Scientific evidence about spaceflight health risks, including sleep and cardiovascular risks.
sources.limitations: Evidence reports support explanations; they are not continuous sensor datasets.

sources.title: WESAD Dataset
sources.supports: Independent testing of physiological signal processing methods.
sources.limitations: Earth-based wearable dataset. Never label its records as NASA or astronaut data.

sources.title: BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset
sources.supports: Independent testing of physiological signal processing methods.
sources.limitations: Hospital-based Earth data; separate from astronaut records and spaceflight measurements.

sources.title: Team-created simulated crew records
sources.supports: Demonstrating daily check-ins, personal trends, missing-data cases and the prototype interface.
sources.limitations: Fictional demonstration data only. Must never be described as NASA-measured or actual astronaut observations.

provenance_rules: Every displayed measurement must identify its source and provenance.
Use the appropriate provenance category: nasa_measured, analog_measured, external_earth, simulated or manually_entered.
Do not combine different people, missions, locations or study populations as if they belong to one astronaut.
Do not describe simulated records as real NASA observations.
Do not interpret instrument radiation readings as personal biological risk or individual accumulated dose.
Do not present trends or prototype indicators as medical diagnoses or validated clinical predictions.
If a dataset has not been downloaded and inspected, clearly state that it has not yet been ingested.
Keep the original source URL and measurement context available wherever evidence is displayed.
